title: Tensor and pullback transition adjunct factorizations on prescribed K-flat complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal C'$ be sites small in the module universe, $B_m\xrightarrow qB_n$ a map of commutative ring sheaves on $\mathcal C$, and $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ a geometric morphism, meaning an adjunction $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$ with inverse image preserving finite limits [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $C_m\xrightarrow{q'}C_n$ be ring sheaves on $\mathcal C'$ and fix isomorphisms $c_j:g^{-1}B_j\xrightarrow\sim C_j$ for $j=m,n$ satisfying $c_n g^{-1}q=q'c_m$. Write $g_j^*L=C_j\otimes_{g^{-1}B_j}g^{-1}L$, with its specified adjunction unit, termwise on complexes. Use sheafified balanced tensor and direct-sum total tensor, with differential $d(u\otimes v)=du\otimes v+(-1)^{\deg u}u\otimes dv$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Let $U_j,V_j$ be integer-indexed flat-term K-flat $B_j$-complexes for $j=m,n$, with arbitrary semilinear chain maps $t^U:U_m\to\operatorname{Res}_qU_n$, $t^V:V_m\to\operatorname{Res}_qV_n$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Denote their ordinary adjuncts by $\bar t^U(u\otimes a)=a\,t^U(u)$ and $\bar t^V(v\otimes a)=a\,t^V(v)$, and their actual derived adjuncts by $\alpha^U,\alpha^V$ under the normalized derived scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Put $K_j=\operatorname{Tot}(U_j\otimes_{B_j}V_j)$ and $F_j=g_j^*U_j$. Give $K$ its transition $t^K(u\otimes v)=t^U(u)\otimes t^V(v)$ and $F$ its transition $t^F(s\otimes u)=q'(s)\otimes g^{-1}t^U(u)$. These are the induced chain maps on these prescribed output complexes.

There are canonical chain isomorphisms
$$\varepsilon:K_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n\xrightarrow\sim\operatorname{Tot}((U_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n)\otimes_{B_n}(V_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n)),$$
$$\chi:F_m\otimes_{C_m}C_n\xrightarrow\sim g_n^*(U_m\otimes_{B_m}B_n).$$
On local tensor generators, $\varepsilon((u\otimes v)\otimes a)=(u\otimes a)\otimes(v\otimes1)$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}((u\otimes a)\otimes(v\otimes b))=(u\otimes v)\otimes ab$. The map $\chi$ is pinned by the equality $\chi((1\otimes u)\otimes1)=1\otimes(u\otimes1)$ on the actual inverse-image unit generators, including all scalar multiples and all source-site objects. In transported inverse-image coordinates it is $g^{-1}u\otimes a\mapsto a(g^{-1}u\otimes1)$.

The ordinary adjuncts of the actual output transitions satisfy the chain identities
$$\bar t^K=\operatorname{Tot}(\bar t^U\otimes\bar t^V)\,\varepsilon,\qquad \bar t^F=g_n^*(\bar t^U)\,\chi.$$
All displayed output and scalar-extended complexes are flat-term K-flat. Under their canonical K-flat localization comparisons these are the derived identities
$$\alpha^K=(\alpha^U\otimes^{\mathbf L}\alpha^V)\,\mu,\qquad \alpha^F=(Lg_n^*\alpha^U)\,\theta,$$
where $\mu$ is the canonical strong monoidal scalar-extension comparison and $\theta:T_{C}Lg_m^*\xrightarrow\sim Lg_n^*T_B$ is the scalar-change mate normalized by insertion of $1$, with $T_B=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{B_m}B_n$ and $T_C=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{C_m}C_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback, lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. In particular, if both input ordinary adjuncts are chain isomorphisms then $\bar t^K$ is a chain isomorphism, and if $\bar t^U$ is a chain isomorphism then $\bar t^F$ is a chain isomorphism; the corresponding actual derived adjuncts are isomorphisms with precisely the displayed factorizations. No normalized whole-system input, replacement of transitions, boundedness, or flatness of $q$ or $q'$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the exactness of geometric inverse image and ordinary scalar restriction to supply the ten functor instances. Apply the normalized scalar comparison to obtain a, a', d, d', its ordinary isomorphism, its unit square, and its localized mate square. Invert its ordinary isomorphism to obtain χ and cancel its inverse in the unit square.

Apply scalar-extension preservation of K-flatness to the given ordinary functor using its prescribed object and map equations. Its objectwise identification with explicit scalar extension and flatness under isomorphism give flat terms. Combine this with the K-flat total-tensor theorem and the inverse-image K-flat and flatness theorems to prove all ten Good assertions. No auxiliary homotopy-derived pair is needed.

Use the existing canonical scalar total-tensor comparison for a functor identified with scalar extension. Its unit-generator equation supplies epsilon on scalar-one homogeneous generators. Linearity of epsilon and bilinearity of the total tensor generator extend the equation to every scalar. Applying the inverse to this equation and multiplying the two scalar factors proves the inverse formula.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), balanced-generator computation of the actual tensor transition.

proof.text: Define tK to be the ordinary transpose of ε followed by the total tensor of the two input adjuncts. The adjunction inverse law proves its ordinary factorization. Its unit equation, ε on unit generators, and naturality of total-tensor coproduct injections prove its asserted formula on every homogeneous pure generator.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), inverse coequalizer comparison; ring-isomorphism transport as in the cited node.

proof.text: Apply the general transposition identity for a commuting unit square to the two ordinary scalar adjunctions and inverse-image functors. The χ unit equation from step 1 is exactly the needed square on each cochain degree. This proves the ordinary pullback factorization for the actual pullTransition.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), unit/Hom-adjunction verification of the actual pullback transition.

proof.text: Apply the same unit-square transposition identity to localization and each normalized derived scalar adjunction. This identifies each derived adjunct with the model counit followed by the localization of its ordinary adjunct. Naturality of the native K-flat tensor isomorphism and cancellation of adjacent model isomorphisms then give the displayed derived tensor factorization, with scalarTensorComparison exactly as defined in the statement.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product): normalized K-flat computation of scalar extension and tensor.

proof.text: Rearrange the normalized comparison's representative equation by the exact inverse-image localization isomorphism to obtain the displayed χ representative equation. Localize the ordinary pullback factorization, substitute this representative equation, and use naturality of inverse-image localization to move the ordinary adjunct across its comparison. The derived-adjunct formula of step 6 completes the displayed derived pullback factorization.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); normalized scalar-change mate as stated in the cited comparison lemma.

proof.text: All factors in scalarTensorComparison are isomorphisms: the K-flat tensor model maps, the computing scalar counits, and Q(ε). Functors preserve isomorphisms, so the ordinary tensor and pullback factorizations preserve isomorphisms of the input adjuncts. Their derived adjuncts are also isomorphisms by the computing counit formula. No extra boundedness, flat coefficient-map, or transition replacement assumption is introduced.
